papers.title: A new hybrid approach combining GCN and LSTM for real-time anomaly detection from dynamic computer network data
papers.abstract: This study presents an innovative AI-based approach for anomaly detection in real-time network traffic. Wireshark, a widely used tool in network traffic analysis, was used in the data collection phase of the proposed model and as a testbed for live anomaly detection. A high-performance hybrid model was developed by combining Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), which are a type of recurrent neural network that perform well on time series data, and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN), which capture the structural relationships and dependencies inherent in network traffic data. The proposed hybrid model leverages the complementary strengths of both architectures: LSTM captures the temporal dynamics of network traffic sequences, while GCN models the underlying graph structure of network communications. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to existing methods in detecting various types of network anomalies, including DDoS attacks, port scanning, and unusual traffic patterns. The model is capable of real-time detection with low latency, making it suitable for deployment in production network environments.

papers.title: Blockchain-based cross-domain IoT data sharing: A lightweight, secure edge-assisted approach
papers.abstract: With the rapid proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) applications across diverse domains, secure and efficient cross-domain data sharing has become increasingly critical. Existing solutions exhibit notable limitations in computational efficiency, comprehensive auditing capabilities, and key management security. This paper proposes a novel blockchain-based cross-domain data sharing framework that addresses these challenges through three key innovations: (1) a distributed key management method utilizing blockchain technology that eliminates single points of failure while enabling autonomous pseudonym generation and key updates; (2) a lightweight cross-domain data sharing protocol based on the Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) that facilitates one-to-many subscription mechanisms without computationally expensive bilinear pairings; and (3) a two-tiered architecture leveraging edge computing that enhances efficiency for resource-constrained IoT devices. Security analysis demonstrates that our proposed scheme effectively resists various attacks while maintaining theoretical security. Comparative performance evaluations confirm that our approach significantly outperforms existing solutions in both computational and communication overhead, making it particularly suitable for diverse resource-constrained IoT environments requiring cross-domain data exchange.
